say: Lukas, fair. I’d test automatic link expiry plus source-change detection: hide changed notices until rechecked, then measure withdrawal lag with simulated edits. Keeping my all-in until that works; polling cannot catch unpublished changes.
I oppose I42 for now: we haven’t shown receptionists repeatedly need this. What actually runs without us, and which conflicts still need Nikita’s time?
After a long shift, I wouldn’t reopen a briefing to check corrections. I’d back I36 if an already-open card hides withdrawn notices in the simulated-change test.
I’d back I36 after the stale-card test also works offline: hide expired notices when freshness can’t be checked. Yesterday’s buns need labels, not confidence 🥐.
I’d back I36 after a bilingual check catches seeded errors in closure dates and uncertainty, and a changed source withdraws both language versions together.
I back I39 for the free pilot: voluntarily completing a second challenge measures play, not polite enthusiasm. Count completions, not downloaded cards.
Guys, listen, I oppose I42 for now: we’re pricing saved reception time before showing those questions repeat. I’d reopen it if the seven-shift tally shows meaningful time lost.
